findings.claim: Re-verified (F3 remains open): the verification-runner profile token is split across the current check set — V_N01–V_N12 use '--profile comet-managed-v2' while 95 other checks use '--profile managed-pilot', the case-plan's 92 original cases use '--profile managed-pilot' and its 12 N-cases carry no intended_command at all, and flow_convergence.profile_source_target names a third token 'foundation/profiles/comet-managed.json' with no alias/reconciliation rule anywhere in the contract.

findings.recommendation: During P3_1 observer qualification, converge on one current-profile token (or add an explicit alias mapping) so the 95 retained commands do not silently target a retired profile at VERIFY time.

summary: APPROVE for implementation scope only. With the coordinator's exact file index I re-read the unchanged artifact (SHA 9784847e...) and independently re-verified it end to end this round: all 15 manifest per-file hashes and 9 in-staged replan hashes match actual bytes; drift-lock's four internal sha256 pins match; the DAG has 39 nodes / 69 unique work packages, is acyclic, has zero dangling references, a single VERIFY sink, and waves that cover every node exactly once in valid topological order with all nodes CURRENT_PROFILE_NOT_VERIFIED; the execution contract has 130 unique checks, all required, all historical_results_may_close=false, all in planned-not-executed states, with every task_ids/implementedBy reference resolving to a real DAG node; scenario coverage is exact and mutually consistent (104 DAG acceptance IDs = 104 spec.md scenarios incl. N01–N12 = 104 case-plan cases all CURRENT_PROFILE_RETEST_REQUIRED with historical_pass_inherits=false = 104 bindings keys = 104-entry aggregation map verified check-for-check). The single-controller boundaries in ADR-0020 and the convergence architecture (no second currentPhase, pure Gate, dispatch-only TeamAI, Runner without business state, Kp blocks archive / Kt blocks completion, fencing on restore, R10 retention, purpose-bound secret references, disclosure-intersection publication, separately gated F10 cross-machine scope) are enforced identically in drift-lock frozen interfaces and the N01–N12 WHEN/THEN oracles. This matches the gated decision exactly: it authorizes implementing the frozen converged profile under existing authorization while runtime acceptance, business-profile enablement, and all external writes/publication stay gated behind the artifact's own VERIFY. The two MINOR findings re-confirmed open (R1-Z1 profile-token split across 95/12/12 commands plus a third token in flow_convergence; R1-Z2 stale pre-convergence IMPLEMENTED labels on three journey_definitions) are forward drift risks inside interfaces explicitly declared 'planned, not executable evidence', are barred from closing anything by historical_results_may_close=false and the all-130-current-PASS completion predicate, and are already owned by P3_1/P3_2 — not blockers. Round-0 visibility dissent (R1-001/CA-001) reflects a round-0 tooling limitation now resolved by the exact file index, not an architecture defect. I would authorize the gated decision now.
